analyst_view.overall: Brest (6th, 18 pts) host Paris FC (2nd, 23 pts) on Friday night in a top-six meeting after both won last weekend: Brest beat Strasbourg 1-0 for a third straight league win and clean sheet, and Paris FC beat Angers 4-0. Brest are still without captain Brendan Chardonnet (calf) and Raphael Le Guen (broken leg), both out for weeks, and the numbers also take off Kenny Lala; creative midfielder Kamory Doumbia missed Strasbourg with an ankle problem and one report (Rotowire, 22 Nov) calls him a game-time decision for Friday. Liam Rosenior's Paris FC are missing defender Nhoa Sangui (counted by the numbers) and, per one lineup site, defender Camara with a hamstring injury, with Chergui doubtful; their top scorer Lassine Sinayoko was rested last time and should be fresh. Ruddy Buquet is the referee, a lenient one at 3.2 cards a game, and the numbers already take about 15% off the cards for him. News is still thin three days out with no dedicated preview yet, and the small things that are new point both ways, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.4 for Brest and 1.5 for Paris FC, and they already count Brest's three clean sheets, Paris FC's 13 goals in six and Lala's absence. Paris FC may be short of two defenders (Sangui, counted, and Camara, from one lineup site only), which could help Brest, but Brest may also lose Doumbia's creativity; those pull against each other, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Brest have won only 13 corners in their last six while Paris FC have won 31, and the numbers already move both sides for that form. Nothing in the team news changes how either side builds attacks, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, down from about 4 now that Ruddy Buquet (3.2 cards a game, below the 3.9 average) is named, and they already count Paris FC's 15 cards in their last six. There is no rivalry here and nothing new on discipline, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. Brest have been winning without creating much, while Paris FC have been shooting more than usual, and both trends are in the numbers' momentum. Doumbia's doubtful ankle could make Brest a little blunter, but it is one report and he may play, so I stay at 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Paris FC have hit the target 35 times in six games and Brest have allowed only 17 in their last six, and the numbers already balance those runs. With lineups not confirmed and nothing big missing that they don't know about, I stay at 8.
